import pandas as pd

# File paths for source CSVs
source_files = [
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length6_78/training_0.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length6_78/training_1.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length6_78/training_2.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length6_78/training_3.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length6_78/training_4.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length6_78/training_5.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length6_78/training_6.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length6_78/training_7.csv",
]

# Read all source files with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
dfs = [pd.read_csv(f, index_col=0) for f in source_files]

# UNION all source tables (schemas are identical)
df_union = pd.concat(dfs, ignore_index=True)

# Ensure columns have correct types matching target schema:
# Target schema types:
# 'movie_display_name': string
# 'movie_production_year': integer
# 'movie_genre_display_name': string
# 'movie_financial_summary_production_budget': integer
# 'movie_financial_summary_international_box_office': integer
# 'movie_annual_summary_tickets_sold': float
# 'movie_video_summary_domestic_dvd_units': float
# 'movie_acting_role_display_name': string
# 'movie_theatrical_release_release_date': string
# 'movie_creative_type_display_name': string
# 'movie_production_method_display_name': string
# 'movie_source_display_name': string
# 'movie_running_time': float
# 'movie_technical_role_display_name': string
# 'movie_production_company_display_name': string
# 'movie_sequel': integer

# Convert columns to appropriate types, handling missing values carefully

# String columns: convert to string, fill NaN with empty string or keep NaN as is (target examples show no NaN in strings)
string_cols = [
    'movie_display_name',
    'movie_genre_display_name',
    'movie_acting_role_display_name',
    'movie_theatrical_release_release_date',
    'movie_creative_type_display_name',
    'movie_production_method_display_name',
    'movie_source_display_name',
    'movie_technical_role_display_name',
    'movie_production_company_display_name',
]

for col in string_cols:
    # Convert to string, keep NaN as is (will be empty string if needed)
    df_union[col] = df_union[col].astype(str).replace({'nan': ''})

# Integer columns: convert to Int64 (nullable integer) to preserve NaNs if any
int_cols = [
    'movie_production_year',
    'movie_financial_summary_production_budget',
    'movie_financial_summary_international_box_office',
    'movie_sequel',
]

for col in int_cols:
    df_union[col] = pd.to_numeric(df_union[col], errors='coerce').astype('Int64')

# Float columns: convert to float
float_cols = [
    'movie_annual_summary_tickets_sold',
    'movie_video_summary_domestic_dvd_units',
    'movie_running_time',
]

for col in float_cols:
    df_union[col] = pd.to_numeric(df_union[col], errors='coerce').astype(float)

# The target expects 'movie_theatrical_release_release_date' as string in format YYYY-MM-DD
# Some source data may have NaN or malformed dates, keep as string, empty string if missing
df_union['movie_theatrical_release_release_date'] = df_union['movie_theatrical_release_release_date'].replace('nan', '').fillna('')

# Final target dataframe with columns in exact order
target_columns = [
    'movie_display_name',
    'movie_production_year',
    'movie_genre_display_name',
    'movie_financial_summary_production_budget',
    'movie_financial_summary_international_box_office',
    'movie_annual_summary_tickets_sold',
    'movie_video_summary_domestic_dvd_units',
    'movie_acting_role_display_name',
    'movie_theatrical_release_release_date',
    'movie_creative_type_display_name',
    'movie_production_method_display_name',
    'movie_source_display_name',
    'movie_running_time',
    'movie_technical_role_display_name',
    'movie_production_company_display_name',
    'movie_sequel',
]

Target6_78 = df_union[target_columns]

# Write the final target table to the specified path without the index
Target6_78.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_78/target_multisource.csv", index=False)
